newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EFTA body ends review of Norwegian state bank.
newsitem.headline: EFTA body ends review of Norwegian state bank.

text.p: The EFTA Surveillance Authority said on Thursday it had decided to close without further action its examination into lending by the Norwegian State Housing Bank (Den norske Stats Husbank).

The body, which seeks to ensure free competition in the four-nation European Free Trade Association, said its review was launched following a complaint which alleged that the operating conditions for the bank involved an infringement of the agreement on the European Economic Area (EEA).
The EEA groups the 15-nation European Union and three members of EFTA -- Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
The authority said the complaint was directed towards loans for new dwellings, which it said are provided without any means-testing of applicants.

"The complainant has submitted that owing to special framework conditions within which Husbanken operates, including annual subsidisation over the state budget and an effective 'monopoly' on providing subsidised lending for housing purposes, Husbanken is shielded against competition from regular banks and mortgage companies," the body said in a statement.

However, it said it did not consider that restrictions or distortion of competition go beyond what is required to allow the bank to perform the services of general economic interest with which it has been entrusted.
